For infections caused by Enterococcus faecalis that are resistant to both ampicillin and vancomycin, the preferred treatment regimen includes Linezolid at a dose of 600 mg administered intravenously every 12 hours. Alternatively, Daptomycin at a dose of 6 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours can be used. 2. For Enterococcus faecalis strains susceptible to penicillin, gentamicin, and vancomycin, the preferred regimen involves either Ampicillin 12 g intravenously every 24 hours for 4–6 weeks or Aqueous crystalline penicillin G sodium 18–30 million units intravenously every 24 hours for 4–6 weeks, combined with Gentamicin sulfate 3 mg/kg intravenously or intramuscularly every 24 hours for 4–6 weeks. An alternative regimen includes Vancomycin hydrochloride 30 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours for 6 weeks, combined with Gentamicin sulfate 3 mg/kg intravenously or intramuscularly every 24 hours for 6 weeks. 3. For native valve endocarditis with symptoms lasting ≤3 months, a 4-week course of therapy is recommended. For symptoms lasting >3 months, a 6-week course of therapy is advised. In cases involving prosthetic valves or other prosthetic cardiac materials, a minimum of 6 weeks of therapy is recommended. 4. For Enterococcus faecalis strains resistant to penicillin, aminoglycosides, and vancomycin, the preferred regimen includes Imipenem/Cilastatin 60–100 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours for at least 8 weeks, combined with Ampicillin 300 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours for at least 8 weeks. An alternative regimen involves Ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg intravenously or intramuscularly every 24 hours, combined with Ampicillin 300 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours for at least 8 weeks. 5. For urinary tract infections caused by Enterococcus faecalis, the preferred regimens include Nitrofurantoin 100 mg orally every 6 hours for 5 days, Fosfomycin 3 g orally as a single dose, or Amoxicillin 875 mg to 1 g orally every 12 hours for 5 days. 6. For intra-abdominal or wound infections caused by Enterococcus faecalis, the preferred regimens include Penicillin or Ampicillin. In cases of penicillin allergy or high-level penicillin resistance, Vancomycin is recommended. For complicated skin-structure or intra-abdominal infections, Tigecycline 100 mg intravenously as a single dose followed by 50 mg intravenously every 12 hours is an alternative. 7. For Staphylococcus aureus infections in adults, the preferred regimens include Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg intravenously every 8–12 hours or Daptomycin 6 mg/kg intravenously once daily. For infants and children (>4 weeks), Cefazolin 50 mg/kg/day every 8 hours is recommended. 8. For neonates (<4 weeks) with Staphylococcus aureus infections, dosing of Vancomycin depends on postnatal age and weight. For neonates ≤7 days old and <1200 g, Vancomycin 15 mg/kg/day every 24 hours is recommended. For neonates >7 days old and >2000 g, Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg every 8 hours is advised. 9. For methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) infections, the preferred regimens include Nafcillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours or Oxacillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. An alternative regimen is Vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day intravenously every 8–12 hours. 10. For methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections, the preferred regimen is Vancomycin 30–45 mg/kg/day intravenously every 8–12 hours, with or without Rifampin 600 mg intravenously or orally every 24 hours. Alternative regimens include Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole 10–20 mg/kg/day every 6–12 hours or Linezolid 600 mg intravenously every 12 hours. 11. For diabetic foot osteomyelitis with a high risk of MRSA, the preferred regimens include Linezolid 600 mg intravenously or orally every 12 hours, Daptomycin 4 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours, or Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg intravenously every 8–12 hours (target trough: 10–20 mg/L). 12. For early-onset prosthetic joint infections caused by MRSA, involving a stable implant and symptoms lasting <3 weeks, the preferred regimen includes Vancomycin combined with Rifampin 600 mg orally once daily or 300–450 mg orally twice daily for 2 weeks. Alternative regimens include Daptomycin or Linezolid combined with Rifampin for 2 weeks, followed by Rifampin and a fluoroquinolone, TMP/SMX, tetracycline, or clindamycin for 3–6 months for hip and knee infections, respectively. 13. For pediatric MRSA infections, the preferred regimens include Vancomycin 15 mg/kg intravenously every 6 hours or Linezolid 10 mg/kg orally or intravenously every 8 hours.
